ambiguities.aspect: Initial/reset state of p and q
readings: p and q are uninitialized (x) at time 0 and remain x until the first clock edge (p at 25ns, q at 55ns), as shown in the waveform.
p and q must be initialized to a defined value (e.g., 0) at power-up, so they are 0 from time 0.
If a is x while clock is high, p follows a and becomes x; q captures x at the next falling edge.
If a is x, the module treats it as 0, so p and q remain 0.

ambiguities.aspect: Clock edge timing vs. a changes (setup/hold)
readings: If a changes at the same time as a clock edge (e.g., falling edge at 115ns), the order is undefined; q may capture the old p (1) or the new p (0), giving different q at 115ns.
The waveform implies clock edge occurs before a changes, so q captures old p. This order is not explicitly stated for all edges.

ambiguities.aspect: Output latency of p and q
readings: p changes combinationally with a when clock=1 (zero delay), and q changes on the falling edge (zero delay), as shown by same-5ns-sample updates.
p and q have a propagation delay of one delta cycle, so at the exact sample time they might still show the previous value.
